claim: On 2022-11-17 Application and Network Load Balancers added cross-zone load balancing settings at the target group level, and on 2022-11-28 Application Load Balancers added the option to turn off cross-zone load balancing.
q: Since when can cross-zone load balancing be set per target group, and turned off on an Application Load Balancer?
scope: Application and Network Load Balancer target groups
note: d124. Current truth: elb-alb-cross-zone-always-on-lb-level, elb-alb-cross-zone-tg-override, elb-nlb-cross-zone-lb-and-tg-level, elb-alb-sticky-not-with-cross-zone-off.

claim: On 2022-11-28 Application Load Balancers added zonal shift, which routes traffic away from a single impaired Availability Zone through Amazon Application Recovery Controller (ARC).
q: When could you first shift Application Load Balancer traffic away from an impaired Availability Zone with ARC?
values: away from a single impaired Availability Zone
note: d124. Zonal shift for cross-zone-enabled NLB (2024-10-11) and ALB (2024-11-22) is dated only by What's New posts that robots.txt blocks; current truth: elb-alb-zonal-shift-cross-zone-enabled.

claim: In November 2022 (2022-11-17 for Network Load Balancers, 2022-11-28 for Application Load Balancers) target group health settings were added: a minimum count or percentage of healthy targets and the action taken when it is not met.
q: When did load balancers add the minimum healthy target count or percentage setting?
values: minimum count or percentage of targets
scope: Application and Network Load Balancer target groups

claim: On 2023-03-22 Application Load Balancers added TLS 1.3 predefined security policies; Network Load Balancers had TLS 1.3 policies since 2021-10-14.
q: Since when do Application Load Balancer HTTPS listeners support TLS 1.3 security policies?

claim: On 2023-11-20 Application and Network Load Balancers added security policies that use FIPS 140-3 cryptographic modules when terminating TLS connections.
q: When did Application and Network Load Balancers add FIPS 140-3 security policies for TLS termination?
scope: Application Load Balancer HTTPS listeners and Network Load Balancer TLS listeners

claim: On 2026-08-04 Application and Network Load Balancers added TLS security policies that comply with RFC 9151 (CNSA 1.0 suite requirements).
q: When did Application and Network Load Balancers add RFC 9151 security policies, and is it examinable?
scope: Application Load Balancer HTTPS listeners and Network Load Balancer TLS listeners
note: d127. Not examinable yet (after the 2026-07-15 cutoff).
ev: AWS Application Load Balancer (ALB) and Network Load Balancer (NLB) now support new TLS-based security policies that comply with RFC 9151 TLS server requirements for Commercial National Security Algorithm (CNSA) 1.0 suite requirements.
Customers who are required to meet CNSA 1.0 TLS security requirements can now use ALB and NLB with RFC 9151 compliant security policies.

claim: On 2023-11-26 Application Load Balancers added the Automatic Target Weights algorithm.
q: When did Application Load Balancers add Automatic Target Weights?

claim: On 2025-11-21 Application Load Balancers added health check logs, delivered to an Amazon S3 bucket every 5 minutes with no charge beyond S3 storage.
q: When did Application Load Balancers add health check logs, and what do they cost?
values: no additional charges beyond standard S3 storage costs
ev: AWS Application Load Balancers (ALB) now supports Health Check Logs that allows you to send detailed target health check log data directly to your designated Amazon S3 bucket.
Logs are automatically delivered to your S3 bucket every 5 minutes with no additional charges beyond standard S3 storage costs.

claim: On 2025-11-20 Application Load Balancers launched Target Optimizer, which enforces a maximum number of concurrent requests on a target with an agent that runs on the targets; its traffic generates more LCU usage than regular target groups.
q: What is ALB Target Optimizer and how does it change the bill?
values: enforce a maximum number of concurrent requests
note: d132. Current truth: elb-alb-target-optimizer-no-sticky-more-lcu. The FAQ gives the Target Optimizer LCU sizes (numbers lens).
ev: Application Load Balancer (ALB) now offers Target Optimizer, a new feature that allows you to enforce a maximum number of concurrent requests on a target.
Once enabled, the feature works with the help of an agent provided by AWS that you run on your targets that tracks request concurrency.
Traffic to target groups that enable Target Optimizer generates more LCU usage than regular target groups.

claim: On 2026-07-23 Amazon CloudWatch Logs added Application Load Balancer access, connection and health check logs as vended logs.
q: When could Application Load Balancer logs first go to CloudWatch Logs, and is it examinable?
values: Application Load Balancer (ALB) logs as vended logs
note: d129. Not examinable yet (after the 2026-07-15 cutoff). Current page: docs/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-cloudwatch-logs.
ev: Amazon CloudWatch Logs now supports Application Load Balancer (ALB) logs as vended logs, improving observability and simplifying debugging for network traffic patterns.

You can configure delivery of Application Load Balancer access logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs, Amazon Data Firehose, and Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) with support for Apache Parquet format.

claim: On 2026-09-03 Gateway Load Balancers added optional TCP Reset packets when a target becomes unhealthy, is deregistered, or a flow's idle timeout expires; before, existing TCP connections kept going to the unhealthy target (fail-open). It is off by default.
q: What did the Gateway Load Balancer TCP Reset option change, and is it examinable?
values: TCP Reset is not enabled by default

changed.was: existing TCP connections would continue to be forwarded to the unhealthy target (aka fail-open behavior)

note: d131. Not examinable yet (after the 2026-07-15 cutoff).
ev: AWS Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB) now supports sending TCP Reset (RST) packets when a target becomes unhealthy, is deregistered, or when a flow's idle timeout expires.
Previously, when a GWLB target failed, existing TCP connections would continue to be forwarded to the unhealthy target (aka fail-open behavior).
TCP Reset is not enabled by default to ensure backward compatibility.

claim: On 2024-11-20 Amazon CloudFront added VPC origins, which restrict access to an Application Load Balancer, Network Load Balancer or EC2 instance origin.
q: Since when can CloudFront reach a load balancer in a private subnet through a VPC origin?
values: Use CloudFront VPC origins to restrict access
note: d109, d130. The older pattern (public ALB plus a secret custom header) is not stated as the old value on any saved page. Current truth: elb-cloudfront-vpc-origins-alb-nlb-private-subnets.
